title: Temple of the Inscriptions

groundCutout.basis: Under the measured lower temple platform and main stair. Retains the independent original hill and the adjacent Temple XIII footprint outside the mask.

buildingCutout.basis: The exact named standing pyramid in the local map. Replace directly overlapping generated geometry for this ruin.

terrainReference.basis: Original source terrain sampled in the plaza immediately north of the main stair. The rear extends into a rising hill.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap named ruin ways and INAH archaeological descriptions. The broader lower base is a documented estimate.
mapIdentity.scope: Named ruin way 160083187 fixes the temple location and angle, the plaza side, and the shared west boundary with Temple XIII. The mapped visible outline is about 40 by 31 m. Published archaeological measurements report about 55 by 35 m for the wider base. The wider lower extent is fitted mainly east of the mapped center while preserving the shared west edge.

note: INAH describes the tall north stepped front, six supporting piers and five doorways, and the surviving limestone stubs of the roof comb. Ruz measured 23.38 m by 7.70 m at the sanctuary, with an approximately 2 m podium and a nine-step stair. Filloy places the sanctuary floor about 24 m over the plaza. The 2007 and 2009 photographs fix the surviving gray limestone and visible north and east profiles.
